summary.oneLiner: First earnings call since IHC (Abu Dhabi) closed a USD 1bn strategic-promoter investment (28.5% now, 43.5% post-warrant-conversion); management used the call almost entirely to lay out a multi-year (through FY30) transformation plan — AUM growth from a clean ₹53,160cr opening book toward ₹2 lakh crore, cost-of-funds-led NIM/ROA expansion, and a 5x branch/employee build-out — rather than to discuss Q4 operating performance in isolation.

one-line thesis: First earnings call since IHC (Abu Dhabi) closed a USD 1bn strategic-promoter investment (28.5% now, 43.5% post-warrant-conversion); management used the call almost entirely to lay out a multi-year (through FY30) transformation plan — AUM growth from a clean ₹53,160cr opening book toward ₹2 lakh crore, cost-of-funds-led NIM/ROA expansion, and a 5x branch/employee build-out — rather than to discuss Q4 operating performance in isolation.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4FY26 / FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Not disclosed on call (no P&L walk-through) | — | Call was presentation-led (IHC transaction + strategy), not a standard results readout |
| EBITDA / margin | Not disclosed | — | |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | Not disclosed for Q4/FY26 itself | — | One-time credit-cost/provisioning charge taken this quarter (see below) |
| Gross margin / NIM | Opening-book ROA ~1.6% (annualized) | — | Base for FY27 NIM of 3.5% guided |
| Order book / AUM | Opening AUM ₹53,160cr, 0 gross & 0 net NPA | — | Down from historical disbursement base of ₹3.6 lakh crore (run down over the years) |
| Cash / net debt / net worth | Net worth ₹19,000cr; capital adequacy 20.2% (~29% pro forma for warrant conversion) | — | Gearing capped at 3.5x–4x by policy |
> **One-off called out explicitly:** management took a one-time provisioning/credit-cost charge this quarter to fully clean the legacy book to 0 gross/net NPA ("dipped into our capital one time"). Expects to recover ~₹7,000cr from amounts already provided for; recoveries are baked into forward projections. Management explicitly declined to call this a "write-off," framing it as terminal credit-cost recognition on the rundown book. Annualized terminal credit cost on the ₹3.6 lakh crore lifetime disbursement base, adjusted for rundown, works out to 1.9%.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **AUM/disbursals:** FY27 disbursal target ~₹30,000cr; Q1FY27 disbursals guided 50–60% higher than Q4FY26 (despite Q1 seasonally being slower), stepping up a further 30–40% thereafter. Longer-term AUM target ₹2 lakh crore (multi-year, through the FY30 plan horizon); one reference to FY29 disbursals of "₹72,000 crores" appeared internally inconsistent in the transcript (immediately followed by "roughly ₹6,000 crores") — treat as unclear/needs verification next call.
- **PAT:** FY27 target ₹1,400cr.
- **NIM:** FY27 starting NIM 3.5%, rising toward ~8% over the plan as cost of funds falls ~150bps over 3 years plus sold-down book spread (asset-light) adds to NIM (AUM–on-book-loan gap of ~₹30,000cr in FY28 widening to ~₹45,000cr).
- **ROA glide path (corrected live on call — original slide had a typo):** FY27 1.8% → FY28 3.7% → FY29 4.4% → FY30 4.4% (steady-state ~4%+, NOT the ~8% originally printed on the slide; management to reissue corrected presentation).
- **Cost-to-income:** currently ~50%, targeted down to ~26% by FY30 (30% ballpark near-term), driven by productivity (loans/person/month from 0.6 currently to 2+; already 2x month-on-month between March and April) and TAT improvement (secured mortgage TAT 5-7 days → 2-3 days).
- **ROE:** targeting high-teens ROE, "best-in-class" ROA/ROE over time — no single target year given with precision beyond the FY30 profitability targets above.
- **Dividend:** policy of minimum 25% payout, targeting 40%.
- **Cost of funds / ratings:** reaffirmed guidance of ~270bps total cost-of-funds decline through the AA→AAA journey (120–150bps captured/being captured in the AA→AA+ leg already executed; another 120–150bps expected in the AA+→AAA leg) — explicitly reaffirmed despite West Asia conflict/hardening global yields cited by an analyst. Domestic bonds already +100bps since the IHC announcement (Sept-2025 to date), with another 60–70bps of improvement expected; international bonds +250bps over the same period (smaller share of borrowing mix — ~90% of borrowings are onshore).
- **Capital structure:** capital adequacy at 20.2% now, ~29% pro forma for warrant conversion (₹3,200cr / $335mn balance receivable within 18 months); gearing capped 3.5x–4x; liquidity policy = higher of 6 months of repayments or 10–15% of borrowings.
- **Network build-out:** branch network and employee base both to grow ~5x from current levels; employee count to reach 8,000 by end of FY27 (from current base), with a longer-term target of 20,000 employees and 1,600 branches, offering 15+ products (only 3-4 products materially scaled today).
- **Book value per share:** current ~₹160/share, target to move past ₹200/share.
order book & pipeline: No formal "order book" disclosure (lender, not a manufacturer/EPC); pipeline framed via disbursal targets above. Growth for FY27-FY28 to be ~80% via existing mortgage-led products, moving toward a ~50:50 mortgage vs. non-mortgage disbursal mix by FY30. Portfolio-mix guardrail: 60% secured, 20% unsecured/semi-secured, ~20% via credit-fund co-origination structures (minor Sammaan balance-sheet stake); 80% of the book to remain retail at all times.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Prime mass-market home loans** (yield 8.5%–10%): sourced with intent to sell down to banks.
- **Affordable housing** (yield 10%–13%): held on balance sheet.
- **Secured business loans** (individuals/SME/corporate/micro-LAP, prime, yield 9.5%–11%): sourced to sell to banks.
- **Affordable/semi-urban/micro-LAP** (yield 11%–13.5%): held on balance sheet.
- **CRE project loans**: co-origination model with credit funds, pari-passu, no credit guarantee; Sammaan's own stake ~10–15% of overall disbursement.
- **New products from FY27/28 onward:** loans against securities and gold loans (both secured; gold loans require a distinct branch network/oversight function). From FY28, wider set of unsecured/other products to be added.
- Asset-light track record: over the last 4–5 years, ~₹1.05 lakh crore ($11bn) disbursed and sold down across 24 bank/non-bank relationships; incremental disbursals target ~30% via co-lending/direct assignment.
- Cross-sell: insurance sold to >90% of borrowers today — cited as a meaningful profitability lever alongside core lending.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Gold loans and loans-against-securities as the next scaled secured products (FY27-28), followed by a broader unsecured product suite from FY28.
- AI/tech integration with IHC group (37 use cases identified) spanning: customer experience/response quality, operational efficiency/automation, portfolio risk/early-warning analytics, collections (bot-driven, personalized), fraud prevention, cybersecurity, and AI-assisted board/governance oversight.
- International rating-agency engagement underway (post the domestic AA+ consensus rating) — could unlock a further ~160bps decline in marginal cost of funds per management's own math (directly doubling the current ~1.6% ROA on the opening book, on their stated logic).
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Cost-of-funds discipline / liability management** — management explicitly frames this business as being about liability management, not asset management; a diversified, long-tenor (3–4yr maturity) borrowing book, a formal gearing cap (3.5x–4x) and liquidity policy (6-months-repayment / 10-15%-of-borrowings) are cited as the durable differentiator versus peers.
- **Terminal-credit-cost demonstrated track record** — cumulative ₹3.6 lakh crore of historical disbursements run down with an annualized terminal credit cost of only 1.9%, and historic deleveraging of ₹1.3 lakh crore net since Sept-2018 — used as evidence of underwriting discipline through a full cycle, which management argues few competitors (including newer AAA NBFCs) have had to prove.
- **Backing/rating halo from IHC** — all three domestic rating agencies (CRISIL, CARE, ICRA) upgraded the company within the first 50 days of the IHC investment closing (CRISIL 9-Apr, CARE 12-May, ICRA same-day as this call), a speed of re-rating management calls unprecedented even internally.
margins & cost dynamics: NIM starts FY27 at 3.5%, expected to expand toward ~8% over the plan (cost-of-funds decline of ~150bps over 3 years plus sold-down-book spread contribution to NIM, e.g., AUM-vs-on-book-loan gap of ₹30,000cr in FY28 rising to ₹45,000cr). Cost-to-income ~50% today, targeted at ~26% by FY30 via productivity gains (0.6 → 2+ loans/person/month) and amortizing the existing centralized/senior-management cost base over a much larger disbursal volume.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Branch/people build-out is the primary "capex": gold-loan branches cost ~₹20 lakh to set up and take ~3 years to reach full productivity; 240 existing branches already being repurposed/sized for the new product suite. Tech investment (CRM/Salesforce upgrade already made ~6 months ago in anticipation) is characterized as expensed through the P&L, not capitalized — flagged by management itself as a specific point to track (no capitalized-cost cushion to the profit targets).
capital allocation: $1bn IHC investment structure: ~₹5,652cr ($592mn) already received (equity issuance + 25% upfront warrant payment); balance ~₹3,200cr ($335mn) due within 18 months on warrant conversion. IHC current stake 28.5%, rising to 43.5% post-conversion. Dividend policy re-established: minimum 25% payout, target 40%. Capital adequacy 20.2% now (~29% pro forma), well above the 3.5x-4x gearing cap — management explicitly says "we have a lot of capital."
risks & watch-items:
- ROA/NIM/cost-to-income targets are aggressive vs. NBFC peer history — an analyst flagged that even the corrected FY30 ROA glide (4.4%) and cost-to-income (26%) targets are rarely achieved at scale by Indian NBFCs; management's confidence rests on cost-of-funds trajectory and productivity assumptions that are not yet proven at the new (non-mortgage) product lines.
- The FY29 disbursal figure in the transcript ("₹72,000 crores... roughly ₹6,000 crores") is internally inconsistent — needs clarification next call.
- International rating-agency upgrades (needed to unlock the AA+→AAA leg of the 270bps cost-of-funds glide) are not yet secured — West Asia conflict and global yield hardening were raised by an analyst as a headwind to that trajectory; management reaffirmed the 270bps target but this is unconfirmed progress, not achieved.
- Slide/data-quality issue this quarter (FY30 ROA guidance printed incorrectly as ~8% vs. corrected 4.4%) — worth checking whether the reissued presentation matches what was said live.
- Competitive intensity: multiple AAA-rated, well-capitalized NBFCs already exist in India (unlike Sammaan's/Indiabulls' earlier AAA era) — management acknowledges this but argues the addressable market (Tier 4-6 "Bharat") is large enough that market share of any one AAA/AA+ player remains modest.
management quality / tone: Confident, promotional tone dominated by the new-promoter narrative (extensive scripted remarks from IHC's Peter Abraam and Avalora's Dalia Khorshid). Gagan Banga leaned heavily on "we've seen cycles before" credibility (2-decade history, historic ₹1.3 lakh crore deleveraging) to justify aggressive multi-year targets. Management proactively corrected a slide error live on the call (FY30 ROA) and volunteered detail on write-off/recovery treatment when directly challenged by a retail investor — reasonable transparency on a sensitive legacy-book topic.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The "opening AUM" framing (₹53,160cr, 0 gross/net NPA, cash-flow tested since a ₹1.35 lakh crore book in Sept-2018) is being used as a clean base on which all forward ROA/ROE math is built — effectively resetting the credit narrative post the legacy NPA cycle.
- Management's own math: a 160bps decline in marginal cost of funds (from international rating-agency upgrades) would roughly double the current 1.6% ROA on the opening book — a useful sensitivity to track as international ratings news flow arrives.
- Productivity claims are already showing in-quarter proof points (loans/person/month roughly doubled March→April 2026) — an early, verifiable leading indicator ahead of the FY27 P&L.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Promoter group is Avenir Investment RSC Limited, described as an IHC subsidiary, holding 28.5%; the deck notes this "is to increase to ~43.5% upon ~Rs 3,198 Crs warrant infusion, subject to conversion by 30th Sept, 2027".
- The growth path is repeatedly framed as "Supported by Balance Sheet Strength and Comfort from IHC Group" / "Operating Strength and Comfort from IHC Group", with 2 IHC Group members on the SCL Board, IHC functional heads in key operating committees (IT/AI & Infrastructure, Risk, HR, Data Science, Marketing, Finance) and SCL's financials consolidating into IHC's.
- Positioned as staying "mortgage/secured-focused overall": 97% of Q1FY27 disbursements are secured loans, with AUM shown 97.1% secured / 2.9% unsecured and disbursals 97.0% / 3.0%.
- Credit standing is a stated pillar: "AA+ Consensus Achieved" domestically (AA+/Stable) with international BB-/Stable, a stated FY28 target of AAA, and a claim of being 3rd-highest bond issuer among AA+ peers during Apr-Aug 2026.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Prime mass-market home loans** (yield 8.5%–10%): sourced with intent to sell down to banks.
- **Affordable housing** (yield 10%–13%): held on balance sheet.
- **Secured business loans** (individuals/SME/corporate/micro-LAP, prime, yield 9.5%–11%): sourced to sell to banks.
- **Affordable/semi-urban/micro-LAP** (yield 11%–13.5%): held on balance sheet.
- **CRE project loans**: co-origination model with credit funds, pari-passu, no credit guarantee; Sammaan's own stake ~10–15% of overall disbursement.
- **New products from FY27/28 onward:** loans against securities and gold loans (both secured; gold loans require a distinct branch network/oversight function). From FY28, wider set of unsecured/other products to be added.
- Asset-light track record: over the last 4–5 years, ~₹1.05 lakh crore ($11bn) disbursed and sold down across 24 bank/non-bank relationships; incremental disbursals target ~30% via co-lending/direct assignment.
- Cross-sell: insurance sold to >90% of borrowers today — cited as a meaningful profitability lever alongside core lending.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: No formal "order book" disclosure (lender, not a manufacturer/EPC); pipeline framed via disbursal targets above. Growth for FY27-FY28 to be ~80% via existing mortgage-led products, moving toward a ~50:50 mortgage vs. non-mortgage disbursal mix by FY30. Portfolio-mix guardrail: 60% secured, 20% unsecured/semi-secured, ~20% via credit-fund co-origination structures (minor Sammaan balance-sheet stake); 80% of the book to remain retail at all times.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **AUM/disbursals:** FY27 disbursal target ~₹30,000cr; Q1FY27 disbursals guided 50–60% higher than Q4FY26 (despite Q1 seasonally being slower), stepping up a further 30–40% thereafter. Longer-term AUM target ₹2 lakh crore (multi-year, through the FY30 plan horizon); one reference to FY29 disbursals of "₹72,000 crores" appeared internally inconsistent in the transcript (immediately followed by "roughly ₹6,000 crores") — treat as unclear/needs verification next call.
- **PAT:** FY27 target ₹1,400cr.
- **NIM:** FY27 starting NIM 3.5%, rising toward ~8% over the plan as cost of funds falls ~150bps over 3 years plus sold-down book spread (asset-light) adds to NIM (AUM–on-book-loan gap of ~₹30,000cr in FY28 widening to ~₹45,000cr).
- **ROA glide path (corrected live on call — original slide had a typo):** FY27 1.8% → FY28 3.7% → FY29 4.4% → FY30 4.4% (steady-state ~4%+, NOT the ~8% originally printed on the slide; management to reissue corrected presentation).
- **Cost-to-income:** currently ~50%, targeted down to ~26% by FY30 (30% ballpark near-term), driven by productivity (loans/person/month from 0.6 currently to 2+; already 2x month-on-month between March and April) and TAT improvement (secured mortgage TAT 5-7 days → 2-3 days).
- **ROE:** targeting high-teens ROE, "best-in-class" ROA/ROE over time — no single target year given with precision beyond the FY30 profitability targets above.
- **Dividend:** policy of minimum 25% payout, targeting 40%.
- **Cost of funds / ratings:** reaffirmed guidance of ~270bps total cost-of-funds decline through the AA→AAA journey (120–150bps captured/being captured in the AA→AA+ leg already executed; another 120–150bps expected in the AA+→AAA leg) — explicitly reaffirmed despite West Asia conflict/hardening global yields cited by an analyst. Domestic bonds already +100bps since the IHC announcement (Sept-2025 to date), with another 60–70bps of improvement expected; international bonds +250bps over the same period (smaller share of borrowing mix — ~90% of borrowings are onshore).
- **Capital structure:** capital adequacy at 20.2% now, ~29% pro forma for warrant conversion (₹3,200cr / $335mn balance receivable within 18 months); gearing capped 3.5x–4x; liquidity policy = higher of 6 months of repayments or 10–15% of borrowings.
- **Network build-out:** branch network and employee base both to grow ~5x from current levels; employee count to reach 8,000 by end of FY27 (from current base), with a longer-term target of 20,000 employees and 1,600 branches, offering 15+ products (only 3-4 products materially scaled today).
- **Book value per share:** current ~₹160/share, target to move past ₹200/share.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- Gold loans and loans-against-securities as the next scaled secured products (FY27-28), followed by a broader unsecured product suite from FY28.
- AI/tech integration with IHC group (37 use cases identified) spanning: customer experience/response quality, operational efficiency/automation, portfolio risk/early-warning analytics, collections (bot-driven, personalized), fraud prevention, cybersecurity, and AI-assisted board/governance oversight.
- International rating-agency engagement underway (post the domestic AA+ consensus rating) — could unlock a further ~160bps decline in marginal cost of funds per management's own math (directly doubling the current ~1.6% ROA on the opening book, on their stated logic).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: NIM starts FY27 at 3.5%, expected to expand toward ~8% over the plan (cost-of-funds decline of ~150bps over 3 years plus sold-down-book spread contribution to NIM, e.g., AUM-vs-on-book-loan gap of ₹30,000cr in FY28 rising to ₹45,000cr). Cost-to-income ~50% today, targeted at ~26% by FY30 via productivity gains (0.6 → 2+ loans/person/month) and amortizing the existing centralized/senior-management cost base over a much larger disbursal volume.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: $1bn IHC investment structure: ~₹5,652cr ($592mn) already received (equity issuance + 25% upfront warrant payment); balance ~₹3,200cr ($335mn) due within 18 months on warrant conversion. IHC current stake 28.5%, rising to 43.5% post-conversion. Dividend policy re-established: minimum 25% payout, target 40%. Capital adequacy 20.2% now (~29% pro forma), well above the 3.5x-4x gearing cap — management explicitly says "we have a lot of capital."

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, promotional tone dominated by the new-promoter narrative (extensive scripted remarks from IHC's Peter Abraam and Avalora's Dalia Khorshid). Gagan Banga leaned heavily on "we've seen cycles before" credibility (2-decade history, historic ₹1.3 lakh crore deleveraging) to justify aggressive multi-year targets. Management proactively corrected a slide error live on the call (FY30 ROA) and volunteered detail on write-off/recovery treatment when directly challenged by a retail investor — reasonable transparency on a sensitive legacy-book topic.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Cost-of-funds discipline / liability management** — management explicitly frames this business as being about liability management, not asset management; a diversified, long-tenor (3–4yr maturity) borrowing book, a formal gearing cap (3.5x–4x) and liquidity policy (6-months-repayment / 10-15%-of-borrowings) are cited as the durable differentiator versus peers.
- **Terminal-credit-cost demonstrated track record** — cumulative ₹3.6 lakh crore of historical disbursements run down with an annualized terminal credit cost of only 1.9%, and historic deleveraging of ₹1.3 lakh crore net since Sept-2018 — used as evidence of underwriting discipline through a full cycle, which management argues few competitors (including newer AAA NBFCs) have had to prove.
- **Backing/rating halo from IHC** — all three domestic rating agencies (CRISIL, CARE, ICRA) upgraded the company within the first 50 days of the IHC investment closing (CRISIL 9-Apr, CARE 12-May, ICRA same-day as this call), a speed of re-rating management calls unprecedented even internally.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- ROA/NIM/cost-to-income targets are aggressive vs. NBFC peer history — an analyst flagged that even the corrected FY30 ROA glide (4.4%) and cost-to-income (26%) targets are rarely achieved at scale by Indian NBFCs; management's confidence rests on cost-of-funds trajectory and productivity assumptions that are not yet proven at the new (non-mortgage) product lines.
- The FY29 disbursal figure in the transcript ("₹72,000 crores... roughly ₹6,000 crores") is internally inconsistent — needs clarification next call.
- International rating-agency upgrades (needed to unlock the AA+→AAA leg of the 270bps cost-of-funds glide) are not yet secured — West Asia conflict and global yield hardening were raised by an analyst as a headwind to that trajectory; management reaffirmed the 270bps target but this is unconfirmed progress, not achieved.
- Slide/data-quality issue this quarter (FY30 ROA guidance printed incorrectly as ~8% vs. corrected 4.4%) — worth checking whether the reissued presentation matches what was said live.
- Competitive intensity: multiple AAA-rated, well-capitalized NBFCs already exist in India (unlike Sammaan's/Indiabulls' earlier AAA era) — management acknowledges this but argues the addressable market (Tier 4-6 "Bharat") is large enough that market share of any one AAA/AA+ player remains modest.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The "opening AUM" framing (₹53,160cr, 0 gross/net NPA, cash-flow tested since a ₹1.35 lakh crore book in Sept-2018) is being used as a clean base on which all forward ROA/ROE math is built — effectively resetting the credit narrative post the legacy NPA cycle.
- Management's own math: a 160bps decline in marginal cost of funds (from international rating-agency upgrades) would roughly double the current 1.6% ROA on the opening book — a useful sensitivity to track as international ratings news flow arrives.
- Productivity claims are already showing in-quarter proof points (loans/person/month roughly doubled March→April 2026) — an early, verifiable leading indicator ahead of the FY27 P&L.

qoq_log.body:
